reading.synopsis: Published posthumously in 1997 at 505 pages, this anthology opens with 'Fair Game,' in which an exhausted Colorado professor's ordinary domestic evening is disrupted by hints of government research -- a characteristic Dickian move of beginning with a mundane, recognizable scene before introducing destabilizing elements. Designed as a more curated, general-audience entry point than the completist Underwood-Miller Collected Stories, the volume's back cover quotes The Wall Street Journal praising Dick's distinctive ability to put readers inside his characters' consciousness, reflecting the growing critical reputation that followed his death in 1982.
motifs: Suburban alienation and altered perception as recurring entry points across the selected stories
The tension between domestic comfort and cosmic or institutional upheaval
reading.significance: As a reader-friendly rather than completist selection, this anthology was designed to introduce Dick's short fiction to the expanding general audience discovering his work through film adaptations and posthumous critical reassessment, rather than to serve specialist collectors.
reading.closing_note: This entry documents the anthology as a publishing object; readers seeking analysis of individual stories, including 'Fair Game,' should consult each story's own dossier elsewhere in this corpus.
